Subject: OrbitFin — closure note, root cause, timeline, and corrective roadmap (summary)

Hi Sasha —

Thanks again for your patience. Below is a concise closure note we prepared for OrbitFin. I’ve included the timeline, root cause analysis, immediate mitigations, and prioritized corrective actions. We’ve also attached the full incident log and the remediation slide deck to the Drive link shared above.

Incident summary (one line)
A short-lived capacity and memory-pressure condition in our model-serving pool caused increased tail latency and elevated error rates for customers routed to a single GPU pool in us-west-2 between 02:12–02:55 UTC on 2027-06-01.

Impact
- Start: 2027-06-01T02:12:08Z; End: 2027-06-01T02:55:19Z
- OrbitFin observed increased 4xx/5xx and failed token responses for approximately 18% of requests routed through the affected pool.
- Scope: subset of customers using cross-model routing to the legacy quantized runtime.

Root cause (summary)
- A change in our internal cache-eviction policy (deployed 05-30) increased aggressive reclaim behavior when memory headroom fell below an updated threshold.
- Under a specific workload pattern (high concurrency with many short sequences and repeated model switches), the cache eviction became synchronous during certain kernel paths, triggering repeated KV cache miss/regeneration cycles and transient memory pressure.
- The memory pressure caused the runtime to throttle request admission while background eviction tasks serialized, which increased tail latency and resulted in error responses for some inflight requests.

Why this escaped pre-release detection
- The test harness used representative throughput but did not mimic OrbitFin’s exact cross-model switching pattern. The gating metrics did not capture the synchronous eviction path because it requires a combination of short latency-sensitive sequences and rapid model variant switches.

Immediate mitigations applied (completed within the incident window)
- Reverted the recent eviction-threshold change in the affected pool (completed 02:28 UTC).
- Temporarily widened admission controls to avoid queueing-induced timeouts (02:35 UTC).
- Applied an emergency patch to make KV eviction asynchronous for the most common kernel path (02:45 UTC).

Timeline (detailed)
- 02:12:08Z — First customer error reports and internal alert fires for elevated tail latency in us-west-2 pool B.
- 02:17:00Z — SRE on-call begins investigation; initial hypothesis around network flakiness ruled out.
- 02:22:40Z — Reproduced increased synchronous eviction behavior on staging using a captured OrbitFin workload.
- 02:28:13Z — Rolled back eviction-threshold change for pool B.
- 02:35:50Z — Adjusted admission control to reduce enqueue latency.
- 02:45:37Z — Emergency asymmetric async-eviction patch deployed to affected binary subset.
- 02:55:19Z — Metrics and error rates returned to baseline; continued monitoring for 2 hours.

Corrective actions (prioritized)
1) Short-term (1–2 weeks):
   - Add a synthetic workload test that mirrors OrbitFin’s cross-model switching and short-sequence patterns (owner: SRE; ETA: 2027-06-09).
   - Pin eviction-threshold config per-pool to more conservative defaults and restrict rollout gating (owner: Runtime Eng; ETA: 2027-06-08).
   - Deliver a formal usage-based credit for the impacted window (owner: Finance & CS; ETA: 2027-06-04).

2) Medium-term (1–2 months):
   - Rework KV cache eviction to avoid synchronous paths in all common kernels; add observability hooks to measure eviction latency (owner: Runtime Team; ETA: 2027-07-15).
   - Expand pre-release harnesses to include multi-model switching scenarios; add a regression test in CI (owner: QA/Runtime; ETA: 2027-07-01).

3) Long-term (quarter):
   - Re-architect cache warming and cross-model routing to reduce regeneration events across frequent variant switches.

Customer-facing commitments
- We will share a concise postmortem deck and a remediation review in a 30-min call (suggested: Thu 2027-06-03 10:00 AM PT).
- We will issue a usage credit for the impacted window and include the calculation in a follow-up email.
- We will share progress updates on the short-term remediation items weekly until complete.

Attachments referenced
- orbitfin-incident-log-20270601.txt (detailed event logs)
- redwood-service-timeline-0601.csv (metric dumps and annotations)
- remediation-plan-0602.pdf (slides with action owners and deadlines)

If you’d like a tighter technical readout (full trace views and kernel-level traces), Dylan can join the remediation call.

Thanks and apologies again for the disruption — we’re treating this with high priority and will follow through on the corrective roadmap.

Best,
